matters.matter: NAND demand attributable to Nvidia's CMX storage architecture in calendar 2027 (above 100 million TB?)
matters.why: This is a memory-supplier demand projection: Nvidia's revenue and margin do not turn on CMX NAND tonnage, and no public release will report CMX-attributable NAND demand as a measured 2027 figure, so nothing settles it on a date.

matters.matter: Whether memory makers' capacity additions keep pace with CMX NAND demand
matters.why: It is vague (no threshold for 'keep pace'), has no settling release or date, and is a supply-side side question about memory makers rather than a separate bet on Nvidia.

matters.matter: The French competition authority's decision closing its antitrust investigation into Nvidia (fine, behavioural remedies or closure) by late January 2027
matters.why: Behavioural remedies on its cloud-AI and GPU practices could touch Nvidia's competitive position, a fine is a direct cash cost, and the authority publishes its decision, so public material settles it on a date.

matters.matter: Level and direction of contract memory prices (DRAM/LPDDR5X, NAND, HBM) through 2026-2027
matters.why: Memory is now roughly a quarter of the Vera Rubin rack's cost, so memory price inflation can squeeze Nvidia's gross margin or rack pricing, and contract price series are published regularly enough to settle it.

matters.matter: Per-rack memory content cost on the VR200 (about $2 million)
matters.why: It is a broker's bill-of-materials estimate that Nvidia does not disclose, so no public material settles it, and it moves with memory prices, making it the same question as the main matter.

matters.matter: Timing of first shipments of the Kyber NVL144 rack system (Rubin Ultra generation): 2028 versus the planned 2027
matters.why: A year's slip in Nvidia's next flagship system shifts when its revenue arrives and opens a window for AMD and Google at the high end, and the first shipments will be announced publicly.

matters.matter: Whether the NVL576 eight-rack system ships in volume at all
matters.why: It depends on Kyber and belongs to the same Rubin Ultra roadmap bet an analyst would track on one card, and 'in volume' has neither a threshold nor a date that public material would settle.
